**Netflix Account Terms of Use**

These Terms of Service are in effect for the Netflix streaming service and apply to all Netflix products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms govern the relationship between you and Netflix, including what you're allowed to do with your account.
* **Content and License**: When you upload content to Netflix, like photos or videos, Netflix can use it to operate, improve, and train its AI systems, as long as you've allowed it to do so in your settings and based on applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Netflix's Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. This policy is linked within these terms.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through private binding arbitration, which means you give up the right to a court trial and join a class-action lawsuit. However, you can opt-out of this provision within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination**: Either you or Netflix can end the agreement under specific conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, you can find Netflix's contact information on the help website.

**Clauses to Consider:**

* **Private arbitration**: This means you can't take Netflix to court or join a class-action lawsuit if there's a dispute. This provision may be less protective for you than a traditional court process.

**Note:** If you're unsure about any of these terms or how they apply to your situation, I recommend reviewing the live document and Netflix's website for more information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.

* **Increased advertising:** Despite purchasing an "ad-free" subscription, users may now see ads on streaming titles, starting from January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones.
* **Arbitration with class-action waivers:** Users may not be able to join class-action lawsuits if a problem occurs, potentially leaving them with limited options for seeking compensation.
* **Binding arbitration:** Users may be required to resolve disputes through private arbitration instead of going to court, which can be a restrictive and expensive process.

**Other Key Points:**

* Users must contact Disney+ through the company's published contact information if they have questions about these terms.
* The updated terms can be found at https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

These are the Terms of Service for PayPal, specifically the User Agreement. This document outlines the rules and responsibilities governing your use of PayPal's services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Relationship with PayPal**: These terms govern your relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services (payment processing, etc.) listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: PayPal uses your submitted content (e.g., your profile picture, feedback, etc.) to operate and improve their services, in compliance with applicable laws and your personal settings.
* **Privacy**: The terms reference PayPal's published **Privacy Policy**, which explains what personal data they collect and process. You can find this policy on their website.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute, you're required to participate in **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers (which limit joining lawsuits against PayPal)**. New accounts have a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Termination**: Either you or PayPal can terminate the agreement if the specified conditions are met, as outlined in the live document.

**Potentially Harmful Clauses:**

* **Mandatory binding arbitration and class-action waivers**: While these may help resolve disputes efficiently, they may limit your ability to pursue higher court judgments or join class-action lawsuits against PayPal.
* **Automatic data use**: PayPal may use your submitted content without express permission, as per clause 3.
* **Termination**: Conditions for termination can be found in the live document, which may allow PayPal to terminate your account without explanation or due process.

**Getting Help and Finding Previous Terms:**

If you have questions about these terms, you can find PayPal's published contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . You can also view the previous version of these terms by visiting https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

Keep in mind that you should carefully review these terms before accepting them to understand your responsibilities and the terms' requirements.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

These Terms of Service govern the eBay User Agreement, which is the agreement between you and eBay.

Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Relationship with eBay**: These terms describe the rules and relationship between you and eBay when using their services.
* **User Content and AI**: You grant eBay permission to use your content (such as listings) to improve their artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: eBay collects personal data and uses it as described in their published Privacy Policy, which is cross-referenced in these terms.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes must be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts if you don't want this.
* **Termination**: Either you or eBay can terminate the agreement under specified conditions.
* **Contact**: If you have questions, visit eBay's published legal contact information at the specified URL.

Some potential concerns for users are:

* The use of **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, which limits your ability to take disputes to a public court. You can opt out of this for new accounts.
* The **class-action waivers**, which means you cannot join a group lawsuit against eBay for any disputes.
* The **limited ability to control your content**, which is used to train and improve eBay's AI and ML systems.

Please note that the Terms of Service do not address some aspects, such as:

* What happens if you're unsure about your responsibility in a dispute
* What information eBay will collect in the future
* Any specific rules or restrictions on your usage of eBay services outside of these terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

**Service Name:** Amazon Conditions of Use (Terms of Service)

These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and Amazon, regulating your use of their products and services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** The agreement applies to the services and products listed on Amazon's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Amazon may use the content you submit to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems (e.g., Alexa). This is subject to your account settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** Amazon's Privacy Policy governs the collection and processing of personal data. It identifies the types of data collected and how it's used.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most cases require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, if you create a new account within 30 days, you can opt out of this provision.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but only according to the terms described in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions, refer to Amazon's published legal contact information.

Some clauses that may be considered unbalanced or potentially damaging to users include:

* **Dispute Resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers might limit users' ability to seek collective action or compensation in cases of systemic issues. However, a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts provides some protection.
* **Content and License:** Amazon's use of user-submitted content for AI training and improvement is standard practice, but users should be aware that their content may be used beyond their expectations. The terms are clear that this is subject to user settings and applicable laws, which may offer some protection.

Overall, the Terms of Service outline Amazon's rights and responsibilities in their relationship with users. While some provisions may be considered unfavorable, users should be aware of these terms before using Amazon's services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AMAZON CONDITIONS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: May 2024 update revised disputes/arbitration to explicitly permit small-claims-court actions, updated language about Amazon services covered, and added clearer references to AI features (Alexa, Rufus) and how generated content interacts with the user agreement.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Amazon to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 .

**Service Name:** Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to your relationship with Apple and cover its various products and services like Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store.
* **Content and License:** Apple uses your content to improve and train its Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) systems, based on your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** Apple's Privacy Policy is referenced here, outlining the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms require binding arbitration, which means you'll resolve disputes with Apple through private mediation rather than going to court. You can opt-out of this requirement within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** Either you or Apple can end the agreement under specific conditions, which are outlined in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Forced Arbitration:** The requirement for binding arbitration may be problematic for users, as it can limit their right to a court hearing. While you can opt-out within 30 days, this might not be clear or easy to do.
* **Data Usage:** Apple's terms allow it to use your content to train its AI and ML systems. While this might be necessary for the company's operations, it's essential to understand how your data is being used.
* **Termination Conditions:** The detailed conditions for termination might not be clear or favorable to users, potentially allowing Apple to end the agreement without adequate notice or explanation.

**Essential Reminders:**

* Familiarize yourself with Apple's Privacy Policy to understand data collection and processing.
* Understand the arbitration requirement and opt-out options, if any.
* Review the detailed termination conditions to ensure you're prepared for any potential outcomes.

These terms are subject to change, and it's always a good idea to review them regularly to stay informed about any updates or modifications.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

response:
**Service Name:** iCloud Terms and Conditions

These Terms of Service outline the rules and expectations for using Apple's iCloud service. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These Terms of Service apply to all Apple services and products listed on their official terms page.

**Content Licensing:** When you upload content to iCloud, Apple can use it to improve and develop their artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems, as long as you have allowed them to do so in your account settings.

**Privacy:** Apple references their published Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data they collect and how it is processed. However, you can find the details about data collection and use by reading their Privacy Policy separately.

**Dispute Resolution:** Apple's Terms of Service require "binding arbitration" (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, which means users cannot join together to sue Apple. There is, however, a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, meaning users can avoid arbitration during this period.

**Termination:** Either Apple or the user can terminate the agreement, but the live document describes the conditions for termination.

**Important Notes:**

* These terms apply to the services and products listed on Snap's official terms page.
* **User-Generated Content:** You grant permission to Snap to use your user-submitted content to improve the service, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference Snap's separate **Privacy Policy**, which outlines what data is collected and how it's processed.

* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement, subject to certain conditions.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about the terms, refer to Snap's **published legal contact information**.

**Potential Concerns for Users:**

* **Private Dispute Resolution (Binding Arbitration):** This means that disagreements will be resolved through a private process instead of court, which might limit your options and potential damages. However, you can opt-out within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Use of User-Generated Content:** While Snap aims to respect your settings and applicable laws, the terms grant permission to use your content, which might raise concerns about data protection and ownership.
* **Termination Conditions:** The terms state that either party can end the agreement, but don't specify what those conditions are. This might leave room for interpretation or potential discrepancies.
* **Reference to External Policy:** The terms reference Snap's separate Privacy Policy, which might not be detailed or up-to-date. Be sure to review the actual policy for more information.

Keep in mind that these terms and conditions may be subject to change, so please review them regularly for updates.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Pinterest Terms of Service (also referred to as "the Terms")

**Summary:** The Pinterest Terms of Service describe the rules governing your relationship with Pinterest. These rules apply to the various products and services that Pinterest offers. If you use Pinterest, you enter into a contract with the company, and these Terms outline what you can expect from the service and what's expected of you.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you create content on Pinterest, you grant the company permission to use that content to operate and improve its services. However, this is subject to your personal settings and applicable law. It's not entirely clear how Pinterest uses this content (e.g., AI/ML training), so be cautious about sharing sensitive information.
* **Sharing data:** The Terms cross-reference Pinterest's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of data collected and how it's processed. Check the Privacy Policy for details on how your personal data is used and protected.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If a problem arises, you'll be required to go through binding arbitration, a private dispute resolution process instead of going to court. However, you can opt-out of this within 30 days of creating your account. This might be limiting your right to seek a judge or jury in a dispute.
* **Termination:** Either you or Pinterest can end the agreement, but the Terms don't specify the conditions.

**Potential concerns:**

* **Lack of control over content usage:** The Terms don't specify exactly how Pinterest will use your content, which could be concerning if you share sensitive information.
* **Arbitration provisions:** The dispute resolution process limits your ability to seek a judge or jury in a dispute.
* **Termination conditions:** The Terms don't clearly outline the conditions for ending the agreement, which could leave you uncertain about your rights.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

**Service Name:** Tumblr

**Summary:** Tumblr's Terms of Service outline the site's terms and conditions for users. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Applicability:** These terms apply to you when you use Tumblr's products and services.
* **Content Use:** Tumblr may use your public content, subject to your settings and the law, to improve and train their AI/ML systems. If you don't want your public content shared with partner companies, you can opt-out in your settings.
* **Privacy:** Tumblr cross-references their Privacy Policy, which explains what data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes are resolved through binding arbitration (a private process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, you should note that arbitration can limit your rights and don't offer the same level of protection as going to court.
* **Termination:** Either Tumblr or you can terminate the agreement under specific conditions outlined in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Arbitration Clause:** While arbitration can offer faster resolution, it may limit your rights and don't offer the same level of protection as going to court. This clause is also a `class-action waiver`, limiting your ability to join a group lawsuit against Tumblr.
* **Data Use:** Although Tumblr will use your public content with partner companies only if you opt-out, the company can still use your data to train their AI/ML systems, which may be concerning for some users.

**Key Takeaways:**

* Review and understand your data usage settings.
* Consider opting out of sharing your public content with partner companies.
* Familiarize yourself with Tumblr's Privacy Policy.
* Be aware of the dispute resolution process and the potential limitations of arbitration.

**Next Steps:**

* Review Tumblr's Privacy Policy to understand their data collection practices.
* Update your settings to control how your public content is shared.
* Understand your rights and options if a dispute arises.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

Here's a plain-language summary of the Terms of Service and the key provisions.

**Service Name:** Dropbox AI features, including Dropbox Dash and AI search/summary.

**Summary of Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** The Terms of Service govern your relationship with Dropbox and apply to the services described on the company's official terms page.
2. **Content and License:** Dropbox uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and potentially train AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
3. **Privacy:** Your personal data is subject to Dropbox's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the categories of personal data collected and processed.
4. **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), which includes a class-action waiver (you cannot join a group lawsuit).
5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.
6. **Contact:** For questions about these Terms of Service, visit the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Potential data exploitation:** Dropbox may use your user-submitted content to train AI/ML systems without your explicit consent.
* **Binding arbitration and class-action waiver:** This means that disputes will be resolved through a private process that may not allow you to join a group lawsuit or seek collective compensation.
* **Terms of Service changes:** The Terms of Service can be updated unilaterally by Dropbox, and you agree to abide by the updated changes.

**Your Rights as a User:**

* You have 30 days to opt out of binding arbitration for new accounts (Steam accounts, which are excluded from this requirement, can opt out anytime).
* You must check the latest version of the Terms of Service regularly to understand changes to your agreement.

**Takeaways:**

* Carefully review the Dropbox Privacy Policy to understand how your personal data is being collected and processed.
* Choose wisely when granting access to AI features, understanding the potential risks of data exploitation.
* Consider taking advantage of the opt-out window for binding arbitration and class-action waiver when opening a new Dropbox account.
* Stay up-to-date with Changes to the Terms of Service to understand your evolving agreement.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DROPBOX TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

**Canva Terms of Use: Plain-Language Summary**

**Service Name:** Canva is a design and content creation platform that offers tools and services for users to create graphics, presentations, and other visual content.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with Canva and apply to all products and services on the Canva website.

6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

This set of Terms of Service is for "Notion" products and services. 

Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to Notion's products and services as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Notion, they can use it to improve their operations, AI/ML systems, and your experience. They'll do this based on your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The terms link to Notion's Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required to use _binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)_, and they can't participate in a class-action lawsuit. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement as stated in the live document.
* **Contact**: If you have questions, see Notion's published contact information.

As for clauses that may be _harmful to the user_: 

* Requiring binding arbitration and class-action waivers might limit your options if you have a dispute with Notion. This includes losing the right to participate in a class-action lawsuit, which can be an effective way to address widespread issues.
* Although Notion says they'll use your submitted content based on your settings and applicable law, this still allows them to use your data to improve their AI/ML systems. Be aware of what data they use and for what purposes.

Please note that if you're unsure about any specific point or legal term, consider reaching out to Notion directly for clarification.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Service Name:** Figma Terms of Service

These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you (the user) and Figma, a company that provides design and development tools. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to all Figma products and services listed on their official terms page.

**User Content:** When you submit content to Figma (like designs or files), the company can use it to operate, improve, and develop their AI/ML systems (like machine learning algorithms) - but only according to your settings and applicable laws. The company will not use your content to train third-party models without your explicit consent.

**Privacy:** Figma cross-references their published Privacy Policy, which explains what kinds of personal data they collect and how it's processed.

**Dispute Resolution:** If you have a disagreement with Figma, you and the company must go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). You can opt-out of arbitration within 30 days of creating a new account, but some people (like users of other Figma-like services like Steam) might not have this option.

**Termination:** Either you or Figma can cancel the agreement, but the exact conditions are described in the full document.

**Contact:** For questions about these terms, check Figma's official webpage for their contact information.

**Potential red flags for users:**

* The terms allow Figma to use your content to develop their AI/ML systems without your explicit consent, which may be concerning for users who share private or sensitive information.
* The mandatory arbitration clause, which can limit your options for seeking help or compensation in case of a dispute.
* The lack of clear information about how your data is processed and protected in the Privacy Policy mentioned in the terms.

Please note that these terms are for information only, and if you have specific questions or concerns, you should consult a qualified legal professional.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

response:
**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service

**Summary:** These terms outline the agreement between you and Stack Overflow when you use its services. They cover how your content is used, how your data is handled, and how disputes are resolved. It's essential to read and understand these terms before using the service.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to products and services described on Stack Overflow's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You grant Stack Overflow a license to use your content (like questions and answers) for its services, AI training, and other purposes. However, there are restrictions on bulk extraction of this content for AI training without a commercial agreement.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference Stack Overflow's published Privacy Policy, which explains what data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes are required to go through binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of court. This means you give up your right to a trial and may have limited options for appeal. You can opt out of this within 30 days of creating an account, but other users may be subject to it.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Arbitration Clauses:** The requirement for binding arbitration and class-action waivers may limit your options for seeking compensation or changing company practices.
* **AI Training Restrictions:** While the terms allow AI training with a commercial agreement, there's a restriction on bulk extraction without one. This might affect how AI models are trained and could lead to biased results.
* **Unclear Termination Process:** The terms don't specify the exact conditions for termination, which may lead to confusion or disputes.

It's essential to review the live document (https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public) to understand the full terms and conditions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

**Service Name:** Quora Terms of Service (Effective 2024)

These Terms of Service apply to your relationship with Quora and describe how you can use Quora's products and services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on [Quora's official terms page](https://www.quora.com/about/tos).
* **User Content:** When you submit content to Quora, we may use it to operate, improve, and train our AI and machine learning (ML) systems, depending on your settings and applicable law.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If a dispute arises, most terms require **binding arbitration** with **class-action waivers**. This means you'll have to resolve disputes through a private process instead of a court, and you won't be able to bring a group lawsuit. However, there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts if you don't want to agree to this.
* **Termination:** Either Quora or you can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
* **Privacy:** Quora's Privacy Policy explains how your personal data is collected and processed. The Privacy Policy is cross-referenced in these Terms.
* **Notice and Contact:** If you have questions about the Terms, check the company's published legal contact information on the new TOS URL.

Some clauses may be considered harmful to users:

* **Use of user data for AI and ML:** While users may have some control over how their data is used, it's unclear how this provision will be enforced. Be aware that Quora may use your submissions to train AI and ML systems without your explicit consent.
* **Binding arbitration and class-action waivers:** These restrictions on dispute resolution may limit users' options if a dispute arises.
* **Automatic termination terms:** The conditions for termination are not specified in the Terms, which may lead to uncertainty or disputes about when the agreement can be terminated.

Keep in mind that these Terms of Service apply to your use of Quora's products and services, and reviewing them can help you understand the terms of your relationship with the company.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Service Name:** Twitch Terms of Service.

The Terms of Service govern your relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services they provide. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Content and License:**

* When you submit content to Twitch, you're giving them permission to use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. This means they can use your content in various ways, like training their recommendation algorithm or generating AI highlights.
* The Terms of Service require you to follow the settings you've chosen, which might affect how your content is used.

**Dispute Resolution:**

* If you have a dispute with Twitch, you might need to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). This means you'll work with a third-party mediator to resolve the issue.
* Class-action lawsuits are typically not allowed, so you might not be able to join a group of people with similar complaints.

**Privacy:**

* The Terms of Service cross-reference Twitch's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how they process it.

**Termination:**

* Either you or Twitch can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions described in the document.

**Important Considerations:**

* The Terms of Service allow Twitch to use your content in various ways, which might not be ideal for everyone.
* The requirement for binding arbitration and class-action waivers might limit your ability to seek justice in a court of law.
* The opt-out window for new accounts is just 30 days, which might not be enough time for some users to make an informed decision about arbitration.

If you're concerned about any of these provisions, it's essential to review the Terms of Service carefully and consider your options.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

**Service Name:**
These Terms of Service apply to the Roblox platform and its related products and services.

**Key Provisions:**
Here's a breakdown of the key points:

* **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with Roblox and apply to the services described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Roblox, they may use it to operate, improve, or train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means that your content might be used in ways you didn't intend or expect.
* **Privacy:** Roblox cross-references its published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how they process it. Please note that Roblox may collect your personal data for various purposes.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms in this set require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means that if you have a dispute, you'll settle it outside of court, and you might not be able to join a class-action lawsuit. However, there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, which allows you to choose a different dispute resolution process.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but the terms will describe the conditions for doing so.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, you can refer to the company's published legal contact information on their website.

**Potential Harmful Clauses:**
Based on the provided information, the following clauses might be considered potentially harmful to the user:

* **Class-action waivers:** This might limit your ability to join a group lawsuit against Roblox if you have a similar complaint.
* **Binding arbitration:** This could prevent you from taking disputes to court, which might be a problem if you're not satisfied with the outcome of arbitration.
* **Use of your content:** Roblox's rights to use your content might be more expansive than you'd like, and you should carefully review the terms to understand how your content might be used.
* **Data collection and processing:** Roblox's Privacy Policy will explain their data collection practices, but you should be aware that they collect and process personal data for various purposes.

Please note that these are just potential concerns and not all users may be affected by these clauses. If you're concerned about these points, it's essential to review the entire document and adjust your behavior accordingly.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

**Service Name:** The Steam Subscriber Agreement, which governs your relationship with Steam (Valve) and applies to the products and services on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms cover your relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services mentioned on their terms page.
* **Content and License:** Steam (Valve) uses your user-submitted content (e.g., game reviews, screenshots) to operate, improve, and "train" their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference Steam's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users are required to resolve disputes through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers (making group lawsuits harder to bring)**. However, new Steam accounts can opt out of this requirement within 30 days. Steam (Valve) is an exception, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement based on conditions specified in the live document.
* **Contact:** Questions about the terms should be directed to Steam's published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns for Users:**

* The requirement for **binding arbitration with class-action waivers** may limit your ability to bring group lawsuits or seek justice through the court system. However, this requirement only applies to most users, and new accounts can opt out within 30 days.
* The use of **user-submitted content** for **AI/ML training** may raise concerns about data ownership and the potential for misuse.
* The **cross-reference to Steam's Privacy Policy** is reassuring as it ensures users are aware of how their personal data is collected and processed.

Overall, these Terms of Service aim to clarify your relationship with Steam (Valve) and outline their rights and responsibilities. While there are some potential concerns, the removal of mandatory arbitration for new Steam accounts in 2024 and the referenced Privacy Policy are positive steps towards greater user protection.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STEAM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: September 26, 2024 update removed the mandatory arbitration / class-action waiver clauses entirely - Valve now requires disputes to be filed in court (subject to venue rules), reversing several years of arbitration-only language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Steam (Valve) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ .

It's worth noting that Epic Games reserves the right to terminate the agreement at any time, subject to certain conditions.
* **Termination**: The agreement can be terminated by either party, as described in the live document. However, the text doesn't provide further details on this.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, you can visit Epic Games' published legal contact information on their website.

Certain clauses may be considered potentially detrimental to the user:

* **Dispute Resolution**: While you may opt out of binding arbitration within 30 days of creating a new account, after that period, it's likely that arbitration will be enforced. This may limit your options for seeking redress in a traditional court.

Overall, these Terms of Service outline Epic Games' rights and responsibilities, as well as the user's obligations and potential limitations. Users should carefully review the terms, including the referenced Privacy Policy and contact information, before proceeding.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

The Terms of Service cover the "DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service". Here's a plain-language summary:

**What the Terms Cover:**
- The Terms describe the relationship between you (the user) and DoorDash.
- They apply to the products and services mentioned on DoorDash's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and Licensing:** DoorDash may use content you submit, like photos or reviews, to improve its AI/ML systems, but only as allowed by your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms refer to DoorDash's separate Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data DoorDash collects and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If a problem arises, you and DoorDash may resolve it through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with some exceptions. Additionally, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either you or DoorDash can end the agreement, but the Terms describe the conditions for doing so.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about the Terms, you can find contact information on DoorDash's help page.

**Clauses That May Be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** Most updates in the Terms continue to require arbitration with class-action waivers, which might prevent you from joining a group lawsuit about DoorDash's policies. This means you may not be able to join others in a lawsuit against DoorDash, potentially limiting your ability to affect systemic change or compensation.

Keep in mind that these Terms may change over time, and it's always a good idea to review them regularly. If you have concerns, it's best to check these Terms directly or contact the company's support team. The Terms of Service themselves state that for questions about the agreement, visit the company's published legal contact information at the provided URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. **Service Name:** Uber US Terms of Use

**Key Provisions:**

* These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Uber and cover the products and services listed on their official terms page.
* The updates you've agreed to on this version of the terms took effect in 2024 and contain some changes compared to the previous version.
* **Content and License:** Uber uses your submitted content, but with your settings and applicable law in mind.
* **Privacy:** The terms point to Uber's published Privacy Policy for more information on the personal data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (note: some exceptions are mentioned).
* **Termination:** Either party can cancel the agreement under the conditions outlined in the live document.

**Potentially Harmful Clauses:**

* The requirement for binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) may limit your ability to seek redress in a public court. This is known as a **class-action waiver.**
* There is no explicit mention of how Uber will address or compensate you if there are any issues with how they use your submitted content.
* Some services or features in the app may not have the same level of protection or support as others.

Please note that the provided Terms of Service do not offer explicit details on how these features and provisions will be implemented or what specific recourse is available to users in cases of disputes or content misuse.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — UBER US TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Uber and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration after the New Jersey Uber Eats arbitration decision, added language on AI-generated trip summaries and driver/rider safety features, and expanded liability sections regarding third-party services.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Uber to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use .

**Airbnb Terms of Service: A Plain-Language Summary**

**Service Name:** The latest version (as of 2024) of Airbnb's Terms of Service governs your relationship with Airbnb.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on Airbnb's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You grant Airbnb a license to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems (subject to your settings and applicable law).
* **Privacy:** Your personal data is collected and processed according to Airbnb's Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.

**Clauses to Flag:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** This clause requires you to resolve disputes through private arbitration, which may limit your ability to go to court. Note that most terms require this, with a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Limited Opt-out Window:** You have a limited time to opt out of binding arbitration (30 days for new accounts).
* **Personal Data Processing:** Your personal data is subject to Airbnb's Privacy Policy, which may collect and process data across multiple categories.

**Additional Information:**

* Airbnb may update its terms, so it's essential to review the latest version regularly.
* For questions or concerns, you can contact Airbnb through the help center (https://airbnb.com/help/article/2908).

Please keep in mind that these terms can be complex, and this summary only highlights key points. If you have specific questions or concerns, it's best to review the full terms or consult with a legal expert.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AIRBNB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Airbnb and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new AnyWhere/Icons experience terms, revised cancellation and refund policies (including AirCover updates), added language on automated/AI-driven listing detection (e.g. anti-party tools), and updated arbitration provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Airbnb to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 .
